mainTopic: אחאי בריבי's question about a pig-like animal following a ewe, then plucking hair from a בכור's neck before slaughter and whether it is allowed on יום טוב
overview: The amud opens with אחאי בריבי's question about a pig-like animal seen trailing after a ewe. The גמרא explains that he is not just asking whether we follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל or רבנן, because a plain lamb would raise that. Instead, he asks a new question inside each opinion: בכורה according to רבנן, and whether the animal may be eaten according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. Both depend on whether a mother animal shows 'mercy' to young of another species, and the question ends in תיקו. A new משנה follows. There, רבי יוסי בן המשולם allows plucking hair from a בכור's neck to clear room for slaughter, or to check a blemish, as long as the hair stays in place. רב rules like him, and students ask רב הונא whether the same plucking is allowed when slaughtering on יום טוב. After confirming רב's ruling through רב חננאל, רב הונא says it is permitted. A second report in רב's name about the same case begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A pig-like animal following a ewe
steps.stepSummary: אחאי בריבי asks what the הלכה is when a pig-like animal is seen trailing after a ewe.
steps.simpleTranslation: אחאי בריבי asked: if someone saw a pig-like animal trailing after a ewe, what is the הלכה?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question is being asked. A pig-looking young animal is following a ewe, and we want to know what follows from that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A young animal following a mother and nursing from her might be a sign that she gave birth to it. Whether it really proves that is a dispute the גמרא brings up in step 3. Here the young animal looks like a pig, so it is even less obvious what to conclude, and אחאי בריבי does not yet say which area of הלכה he is asking about.

keyTerms.meaning: A title of honor, 'the distinguished one'
Pig (here an animal that looks like a pig)
Trailing after, attached to (like a nursing young)
Ewe, a female sheep
What is the law?

phrases.english: (asked) by Aḥai the Distinguished:
phrases.notes: The word 'asked' comes just before this line, at the end of the previous section.

phrases.english: If one saw a pig trailing after a ewe,
phrases.notes: It is a young animal that looks like a pig, following the ewe the way a nursing baby would.

phrases.english: what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: רָאָה חֲזִיר שֶׁכָּרוּךְ אַחַר רָחֵל, מַהוּ
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the halachic outcome when a pig-like animal follows a ewe?

steps.title: What exactly is he asking?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the real point of אחאי's question is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the question he is raising?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what אחאי is really trying to find out. This is a setup line for the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His question did not say whether it is about בכורה, eating, or something else. Before answering, the גמרא needs to pin down the question.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he asking about? What is his doubt?

phrases.english: What is the dilemma he is raising?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the question in step 1 means
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which area of הלכה, and which point of doubt, the question is about

steps.title: If it were only about whom we follow, ask about a lamb
steps.stepSummary: If the question were only whether the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל or רבנן about בכורה, a normal lamb would raise it just as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he is asking about בכורה, and his doubt is whether the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל or רבנן, then let him ask about a lamb!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one reading of the question and then attacks it. That reading would make the strange pig detail pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבנן already disagree about whether nursing proves that the mother gave birth. If אחאי only wanted to know which side we follow, an ordinary lamb nursing from a ewe asks that question exactly. So the pig-like detail must be adding something new.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say, suppose
Firstborn status of an animal
The final law
A lamb
Let him ask (instead) about…

phrases.english: If we say it is about the firstborn status,
and he is asking

phrases.aramaic: אִי הִלְכְתָא כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: whether the law follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
or whether the law follows the Rabbis,
then let him ask about a lamb!
phrases.notes: A plain lamb nursing from a ewe would raise that same dispute, so why bring in a pig?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests one meaning of the question and rejects it
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that אחאי only wants to know whether to follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל or רבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That doubt could be asked with an ordinary lamb, so the pig-like detail would add nothing

steps.title: Two questions, one for each opinion
steps.stepSummary: The question about בכורה follows רבנן, and the question about eating follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he asked, it was about בכורה according to רבנן, and about eating according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that אחאי was not asking which opinion we follow. He was asking a new question that comes up inside each opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate questions. For רבנן, the question is whether the ewe's later offspring counts as a firstborn. For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the question is whether the pig-like animal may be eaten. The next two steps explain each one.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the view of
Eating, whether it is permitted to eat

phrases.english: When he raised the question,
it was about firstborn status, according to the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: לַאֲכִילָה וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל.
phrases.english: and about eating, according to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the question so it applies within each opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question was only about which opinion is the הלכה
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a new question for each side: בכורה for רבנן and eating for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל

steps.title: The בכורה question according to רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רבנן say a mother animal may nurse a young that is not hers. Does that apply only to young of her own kind, or to other kinds too?
steps.simpleTranslation: About בכורה: even רבנן, who say an animal shows mercy, may hold that it shows mercy only to its own kind and not to another kind. Or perhaps it shows mercy to another kind as well?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the בכורה side of the question according to רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבנן, a nursing lamb does not prove the ewe gave birth, because she may be nursing another ewe's lamb out of mercy. If that mercy covers only her own kind, then a pig-like young following her must be her own baby. That would prove she already gave birth, so her next offspring is not a firstborn. If her mercy covers other kinds too, nothing is proven.

keyTerms.meaning: Shows mercy, takes pity (here, nursing a young that is not hers)
Of her own kind or species
Or perhaps
Also

phrases.english: About firstborn status:
even according to the Rabbis, who say she shows mercy,
perhaps she shows mercy only to her own kind,
but to one not of her kind, she does not,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא דְּלָא מִינַהּ נָמֵי מְרַחֲמָא?
phrases.english: or perhaps she shows mercy to one not of her kind as well?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first half of the answer in step 4
steps.sheelahInformationSought: According to רבנן, does a mother animal's mercy reach young of a different species?
steps.confusionAlert: The ewe herself is not the one being called a בכור. The question is whether her next offspring counts as a firstborn, which depends on whether she already gave birth.

steps.title: The eating question according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: Even if רבן שמעון בן גמליאל agrees that a mother who gave birth shows mercy, maybe it is only to her own kind. Then the pig-like animal is hers and may be eaten. If she shows mercy to other kinds too, it might be a real pig.
steps.simpleTranslation: About eating: even according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, if you say he holds that a mother who gave birth shows mercy, perhaps it is only to her own kind and not to another kind. Or perhaps she shows mercy to another kind as well?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the eating side of the question according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a mother shows mercy only to her own kind, the pig-like animal must have been born from the ewe. Then it is a kosher animal that only looks like a pig. If she may show mercy to other kinds too, the animal may be a real pig, and it may not be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: If you will say, even if you assume
He holds
A mother animal that has given birth
Not of her own kind

phrases.english: About eating:
even according to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
if you say that he holds:
a mother that gave birth shows mercy to her own kind,
but to one not of her kind, she does not;
phrases.notes: If so, the pig-like animal must really be her baby, so it is kosher.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא: דְּלָאו מִינַהּ נָמֵי מְרַחֲמָא?
phrases.english: or perhaps she shows mercy to one not of her kind as well?

steps.triggerLanguage: לַאֲכִילָה, וַאֲפִילּוּ לְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second half of the answer in step 4, parallel to step 5
steps.sheelahInformationSought: According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, does a mother's mercy reach another species, which decides whether the pig-like animal may be eaten?

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends with תיקו: the question is left unanswered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds no answer, so it leaves the question open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither side gets a ruling. We do not know whether a mother animal shows mercy to a young animal of another species, for either the בכורה question or the eating question.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question stays unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: אחאי's question works inside each opinion. For רבנן it is about בכורה, and for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל it is about eating. Both turn on whether a mother's 'mercy' reaches another species, and the question ends in תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes both halves of the question without a ruling
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: It stays unknown whether a mother animal shows mercy to young of another species

steps.title: Clearing hair from a firstborn's neck before slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בן המשולם allows plucking hair from a בכור's neck to clear room for slaughter, and plucking hair to check a blemish, as long as the hair is not moved away.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי יוסי בן המשולם says: Someone slaughtering a בכור may clear a spot with a cleaver on both sides of the neck and pluck out the hair, as long as he leaves the hair in its place. He may also pluck hair to see where a blemish is.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It teaches how to deal with the hair on a בכור's neck when slaughtering it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Shearing a בכור is forbidden, but the slaughterer needs a clear spot on the neck. רבי יוסי בן המשולם allows plucking the hair with the knife, but the hair must stay mixed in with the rest so it does not look like shearing. Plucking is also allowed so a blemish can be checked.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn male animal, which is holy and may not be sheared
A cleaver, a heavy butcher's knife
Plucks or pulls out
A blemish, which can allow a בכור to be slaughtered outside the בית המקדש

steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of the sugya asks why this plucking is allowed. The answer decides whether it is also allowed on יום טוב.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Mishnah: Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam says:
One who slaughters the firstborn,
makes a space with a cleaver on this side and that side,
phrases.notes: He is clearing a spot on the neck where the knife will cut.

phrases.english: and plucks out the hair,
as long as he does not move it from its place,
phrases.notes: The plucked hair stays mixed in with the rest, so it does not look like he sheared the animal.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן תּוֹלֵשׁ אֶת הַשֵּׂעָר לִרְאוֹת מְקוֹם מוּם.
phrases.english: and likewise he plucks the hair to see the place of a blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the תיקו that ended the previous sugya.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When slaughtering a בכור, one may pluck neck hair with a cleaver if he leaves it in place, and may pluck hair to check a blemish.

steps.title: רב rules like רבי יוסי בן המשולם
steps.stepSummary: רב says the הלכה follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב says: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with רב's ruling that we follow the משנה's view. This ruling sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב confirms that plucking hair from a בכור's neck before slaughter is allowed in practice. The next question asks how far this ruling reaches.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the opinion of...

phrases.english: Gemara: Rav says:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical ruling on the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם.

steps.title: Does the same apply on a festival? First possibility
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא is asked about plucking hair to slaughter on יום טוב. Maybe רבי יוסי בן המשולם holds plucking is not shearing, so it is allowed for a בכור but forbidden on יום טוב as uprooting.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רב הונא: What about the parallel case on יום טוב? Is רבי יוסי בן המשולם's reason that plucking is not shearing? If so, on יום טוב it is forbidden, because plucking counts as uprooting something from where it grows.
steps.whatsHappening: Students ask רב הונא whether one may pluck neck hair when slaughtering on יום טוב. They give the first way to understand רבי יוסי בן המשולם's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If plucking is simply not shearing, then with a בכור there was never a problem. On יום טוב, though, plucking is its own forbidden מלאכה, uprooting something from where it grows. So on this reading, plucking is allowed for a בכור but forbidden on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: The parallel case, here clearing hair before slaughtering on יום טוב
Shearing
Uprooting something from where it grows, a forbidden מלאכה

steps.confusionAlert: The same act of plucking can be fine for a בכור but forbidden on יום טוב. Each case has a different prohibition: shearing for a בכור, uprooting for יום טוב.

phrases.english: They asked Rav Huna:
What about the parallel case on Yom Tov?
phrases.notes: He means slaughtering any regular animal on יום טוב and clearing the neck hair the same way.

phrases.english: Is the reason of Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam
because he holds
that plucking is not the same as shearing,
and on Yom Tov it is forbidden,
since it counts as uprooting something from where it grows.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעוֹ מִינֵּיהּ מֵרַב הוּנָא: כְּנֶגְדּוֹ בְּיוֹם טוֹב מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רב's ruling and asks whether it also applies to יום טוב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is plucking hair before slaughter allowed on יום טוב? It depends on why רבי יוסי בן המשולם permitted it. Side one: plucking is not shearing, so on יום טוב it is forbidden as uprooting.

steps.title: Second possibility: an unintended act
steps.stepSummary: Or maybe plucking is shearing, but it is allowed because the slaughterer does not intend it. Then it would also be allowed on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps רבי יוסי בן המשולם holds that plucking does count as shearing. He allows it only because it is a דבר שאין מתכוין, something the person does not intend. On יום טוב, a דבר שאין מתכוין is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The question continues with the second way to understand רבי יוסי בן המשולם's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here plucking is a kind of shearing, but the slaughterer only wants a clear spot and does not intend to pluck. An unintended act is allowed, and that same rule applies on יום טוב. So on this reading, plucking would be allowed on יום טוב too.

keyTerms.meaning: An act done for a permitted goal, where the forbidden result is not intended
Or perhaps, which introduces the other side of a question

phrases.english: Or perhaps, in general,
Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam holds
that plucking is the same as shearing,
and this is the reason he permits it:
because it is an unintended act,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְיוֹם טוֹב דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין מִתְכַּוֵּין מוּתָּר?
phrases.english: and on Yom Tov an unintended act is permitted?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִלְמָא בְּעָלְמָא סָבַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite side of the question from step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Side two: plucking is shearing but allowed as a דבר שאין מתכוין. If so, it is also allowed on יום טוב.

steps.title: רב הונא sends them to check רב's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא tells them to ask רב חננאל whether רב really ruled like רבי יוסי בן המשולם. If he did, רב הונא will answer their question.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said to them: Go ask רב חננאל. If he says the הלכה follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם, I will answer your question.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא does not answer right away. He sends them to confirm רב's ruling first, which sets up his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's answer depends on whether רב truly ruled like רבי יוסי בן המשולם. So he first wants to confirm that report from רב חננאל, who learned from רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Go ask him
I will resolve it for you

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: זִילוּ שַׁיְילוּהּ לְרַב חֲנַנְאֵל,
phrases.english: He said to them: Go ask Rav Chananel;

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמַר הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם,
phrases.english: if he says the halacha follows Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam,
phrases.notes: He means: if רב חננאל confirms that רב said this.

phrases.english: I will resolve it for you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: זִילוּ שַׁיְילוּהּ לְרַב חֲנַנְאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the question by making the answer depend on confirming רב's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא will resolve the question once רב's ruling is confirmed.

steps.title: רב חננאל confirms רב's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב חננאל confirms that רב said the הלכה follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם.
steps.simpleTranslation: They went and asked him. He told them: This is what רב said: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם.
steps.whatsHappening: The students do what רב הונא said, and רב חננאל confirms רב's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now it is certain that רב ruled like רבי יוסי בן המשולם. That is the condition רב הונא needed before answering.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what רב said

phrases.english: They went and asked him;
he said to them: This is what Rav said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתוֹ שַׁיְילוּהּ, אֲמַר לְהוּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַב
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, רב ruled that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם.

steps.title: רב הונא rules: allowed on a festival
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that plucking neck hair before slaughtering on יום טוב is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: They came back to רב הונא. He told them: In the parallel case on יום טוב, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא now answers the original question: one may pluck the hair when slaughtering on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying it is permitted fits the second possibility in step 11: plucking is allowed because it is an unintended act, and that works on יום טוב too. The גמרא does not explain step by step how רב's ruling led רב הונא to this answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Before him
Permitted

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא rules that plucking hair to clear a spot for slaughter is permitted on יום טוב, just as it is for a בכור.

phrases.english: They came before Rav Huna;

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: כְּנֶגְדּוֹ בְּיוֹם טוֹב מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: he said to them: The parallel case on Yom Tov is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: כְּנֶגְדּוֹ בְּיוֹם טוֹב מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the answer רב הונא promised once רב's ruling was confirmed.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Plucking hair before slaughter on יום טוב is permitted.

steps.title: Another report in רב's name begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting רב חנניה בר שלמיא in רב's name about the same case on יום טוב, as support.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רב חנניה בר שלמיא said in the name of רב: In the parallel case on יום טוב...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts bringing a second report in רב's name about this same case. The ruling itself comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'it was also stated' tell us this report backs up what came before. The quote continues on the next amud, where the actual ruling appears.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated, which introduces a supporting report
